I am 70 years old now, and I have been farming these 9 mu for half a century. With only my wife and me in the household, I have learned to be practical. I studied agriculture when I was young, so I understand the science — but I also know that at our age, we cannot take on too much labor, and we cannot afford to waste money on inputs that do not pay back.

This year, I will plant 6 mu in the wheat-maize double crop and 3 mu in cotton. Wheat and maize give us grain security and steady income, while cotton brings cash — but cotton is heavy work with all the spraying and hand-picking, so 3 mu is enough for two old people.

For the winter wheat on those 6 mu, I will use an improved variety that I know performs well here. I will rotary till before planting in mid-October. I will apply about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu, along with 4 kg of phosphorus and 3 kg of potassium as base fertilizer. I know from my training that balanced nutrition matters, especially on our soils. I will irrigate three times: at planting, at jointing, and at grain filling. That is what my neighbors do, and it has worked for me. I expect about 1000 kg per mu if the weather cooperates. I will spray pesticides four times to control weeds and aphids.

After wheat harvest in early June, there is almost no time — I will plant summer maize using hybrid seed with no-tillage, sowing directly into the wheat stubble. The hybrid vigor is worth the cost. I will apply 10 kg N per mu and a little P and K. With only two people, no-tillage saves us critical days. I will irrigate twice — once if it is dry at planting, and again at the big trumpet leaf stage. Three pesticide sprays should be enough. I expect around 1050 kg per mu.

For cotton on the 3 mu, I will rotary till in April and plant an improved variety in mid-to-late April. Cotton needs nitrogen but not too much — about 10 kg per mu, or it grows too tall and drops bolls. I will add 3 kg P and 2 kg K. I will irrigate twice, and I know I must spray about 15 times for bollworm, aphids, and mites. It is a lot of work, but 3 mu is manageable. I expect about 550 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I am not trying to maximize every yield — I am trying to avoid a bad year while keeping our costs and labor within what two 70-year-olds can handle.
